Olkusz Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Olkusz, Poland

Not demolished. Olkusz's original Jewish cemetery (see the Olkusz New Jewish Cemetery record for the town's fuller community history), likely established after 1584 and expanded in 1648, remained in use into the early 20th century. Germans repurposed some tombstones for construction during WWII; postwar, the grounds were used as pasture, further looted for matzevot, and partly paved over for a road. Poland formally closed the cemetery on November 4, 1964. Most surviving tombstones were rediscovered scattered around town in 2006 and relocated here, though not to their original burial spots; documentation appears in the book 'Stary cmentarz żydowski w Olkuszu' by Michałowska-Mycielska, Rozmus, and Rozmus.
